notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; the hardware backend was not run and no hardware was attached. The gate did not install or import the upstream package: rware needs gymnasium, numpy, networkx and pyglet, so the fake backend is the package's own pure Python one-agent RWARE re-implementation (fake.py); it was not compared with a run of the upstream environment, and the sim backend (gymnasium.make) was not run. The registered layout has one agent; upstream Warehouse.step returns one reward per agent as a list while the Gymnasium bridge carries one scalar reward, so the fake returns that single value as a float. The bridge publishes a Tuple action space structurally but derives no per-element limit, so SAFE-014 is not applicable (G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE) and an action outside 0..4 fails with MHS.DEVICE.FAULTED instead of MHS.SAFETY.ENVELOPE_VIOLATION; the fake validates the action. Expected warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only sets the seed of the next reset, so it makes no native call), three G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived integer inputs seed (reset), seed (seed) and ticks (step), and G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE. The fidelity is F0 with timestep_ms 0: the environment is a discrete grid world with no physical timestep. No operator-required limits and no extension ids, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
